title: Motor mount 9×9mm
detail: Mounting holes spaced 9×9mm apart (2-hole on some, 4-hole on others) — the standard for small motors used in Tiny Whoop / Toothpick drones. Frames in this class are drilled to match.

title: Motor mount 12×12mm
detail: The most common standard for 5" motors, both freestyle and racing. 4-hole pattern spaced 12×12mm, uses M3 screws.

title: Motor mount 16×16mm
detail: The standard for motors on 7"+ drones and heavy-lift builds. 4-hole pattern spaced 16×16mm, built to handle higher torque.

title: Push-on / pinch-collet props
detail: Props press directly onto the motor shaft with no nut. Suited to low-power motors with modest centrifugal force. Check the prop's bore size matches the motor shaft diameter exactly (e.g. 0.8mm, 1.5mm).

title: M5 screw-on props
detail: Props have a center bushing secured with an M5 nut (some use directional prop nuts for CW/CCW rotation). This is the dominant standard across all 5"+ drones.

title: FC/ESC stack 20×20mm
detail: The 20×20mm square mounting-hole standard for compact flight controllers and ESCs. Used on weight-conscious builds.

title: FC/ESC stack 30.5×30.5mm
detail: The most common mounting-hole standard on the market today, used mainly on 5" frames. Adapter plates are available to fit a 20×20mm stack if you want to mix sizes.

title: XT30 connector
detail: Smaller than XT60 with a lower continuous-current rating. Suited to lightweight builds that don't draw much current, like Toothpicks or ultralight 5" builds.

title: XT60 connector
detail: The most common connector on 5" drones, both freestyle and racing. Handles higher continuous current than XT30, plenty for a typical build.

title: XT90 connector
appliesTo: Large packs 3000mAh+ 6S and up, or high current draw
detail: The largest connector in this group with the highest continuous-current rating. Used on builds that draw sustained high current — big-pack long-range setups or heavy-lift builds carrying significant payload.

title: U.FL / MMCX VTX connector
appliesTo: Builds with the VTX built into the FC stack
detail: Smaller and more delicate than SMA, used on whoop/micro builds where space is tight. Be careful with repeated connect/disconnect since these connectors are more fragile.

title: SMA / RP-SMA VTX connector
detail: Sturdier and easier to swap antennas on. The standard for standalone VTX on 5"+ drones — double-check whether it's SMA or RP-SMA, since the thread polarity is reversed between them.
